sentiment.rationale: The document shows a genuine operational turnaround: revenue swung from $15.2B to $23.9B, operating cash flow from -$3.45B to +$1.33B, and core EPS from -$5.90 to +$9.92. Management provided explicit positive free cash flow guidance of $1B-$3B for 2026, a clear improvement from -$1.9B in 2025. However, the quarter's results were heavily boosted by a $9.6B one-time gain on the Digital Aviation Solutions sale, and management acknowledged ongoing risks on development programs (KC-46A charge, 777X engine issue) and structural headwinds (customer considerations, excess advances). The forward guidance raise is real but tempered by these factors, warranting a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: Q4 2025 revenue of $23.9 billion, up 57% from $15.2 billion in Q4 2024. Full year 2025 revenue of $89.5 billion, up 34% from $66.5 billion in 2024.
summary.eps: Q4 2025 GAAP diluted EPS of $10.23, up from ($5.46) in Q4 2024. Core EPS (non-GAAP) of $9.92, up from ($5.90). Full year 2025 GAAP diluted EPS of $2.48, up from ($18.36). Core EPS of $1.19, up from ($20.38).
summary.guidance: 2026 free cash flow guidance of $1 billion to $3 billion, with operating cash flow of ~$5B-$7B and CapEx of ~$4B. Management expects positive free cash flow for the full year 2026, with first half a use of cash and second half turning positive. Long-term, management believes $10 billion free cash flow is 'very attainable.'
summary.margin: Q4 2025 GAAP operating margin of 36.7% (vs. -24.7% in Q4 2024), heavily boosted by the $9.6B gain on sale. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of 35.6% (vs. -26.5%). Full year GAAP operating margin of 4.8% (vs. -16.1%). Core operating margin of 3.6% (vs. -17.8%).
key_risks: KC-46A program: $565 million charge in Q4 driven by higher production support and supply chain costs, with risk of additional charges.
777X engine durability issue identified during inspection, though management does not expect it to impact 2027 delivery.
Delayed certification of 737-7 and 737-10 (still anticipated in 2026) and 777-9 (first delivery in 2027).
Customer considerations and excess advances on 737 and 787 programs due to prior delivery delays, expected to impact cash flow for several years.
Spirit AeroSystems integration risk and $1 billion negative cash flow impact in 2026.
DOJ payment expected in 2026, a one-time cash outflow.
Tariff and trade barrier risks, particularly regarding deliveries into China and Europe.
Fixed-price development program risk on BDS, with potential for additional charges.
key_opportunities: Record total company backlog of $682 billion, including record backlogs at all three segments.
Commercial Airplanes backlog of $567 billion with over 6,100 airplanes, sold firm into the next decade.
737 production rate increase to 42 per month, with plans to go to 47 later in 2026 and eventually to 52.
787 production stabilizing at 8 per month, with planned increase to 10 per month later in 2026.
Defense, Space & Security record backlog of $85 billion, with 26% from international customers.
Global Services record annual orders of $28 billion and record backlog of $30 billion.
Boeing expects to return to historical performance levels at BDS as it transitions to new contracts with tighter underwriting standards.
Management believes $10 billion free cash flow is 'very attainable' in the long term.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Kelly Ortberg stated 'We made significant progress on our recovery in 2025 and have set the foundation to keep our momentum going in the year ahead,' and Jay Malave said 'a strong foundation was set in 2025, and we're focused on elevating our performance in 2026 and delivering on the long-term potential of this business.'

review_flags.reason: The score of 0.25 is based on a genuine operational turnaround and positive free cash flow guidance, but the quarter's results were heavily distorted by a $9.6B one-time gain. A reviewer should confirm that the forward guidance raise (FCF $1B-$3B vs. -$1.9B) is considered organic enough to warrant a positive score, and that the structural risks (KC-46A, 777X engine, customer considerations) are appropriately discounted.
